findings.conclusion: One RowProjection is constructed after the unchanged columns lookup for one spool/table/input side. It borrows the immutable columns vector, lazily inserts each original key in original order, and updates existing slots. It is not a schema cache and does not cross tables or sides.

All five original ValueRef conversion arms are unchanged: strict UTF8 errors, exact integer and REAL json! conversion, NULL, and original BLAKE3 blob-digest object. The legacy project_row wrapper retains owned Value::Object output. No normalization, excluded field, table set, deduplication or hash-equality shortcut was added.

The new serializer receives the same Map that Value::Object serializes. Column insertion order remains unchanged, including preserve_order builds; ordinary Map ordering also remains unchanged. The original equal_rows fallback, signed-zero behavior, byte sorting, ordinals and duplicate retention are unchanged.

An owned String is produced before values are cleared. Only key storage/map nodes survive; CanonicalInsert never borrows projector values. Conversion failures clear partial/prior values and propagate the same error. Serialization failure clears values before propagation. Production spool still stops at the first error; helper recovery controls introduce no runtime retry.

Row-count admission and check_row_size still precede conversion. Serialized row/cumulative byte bounds, checked arithmetic, ordinal creation, CanonicalInsert 64/8/1 and 64KiB buffering, scratch transaction commit and disposal remain original bytes. No budget was widened.

The two added tests contain literal expected JSON independently of SQL conversion, including integer extrema, signed zero, Unicode/control characters, NULL and fixed empty-BLOB digest; repeated serialization and separate layouts are checked. The invalid-UTF8 control exercises partial updates, original error text and clearing. Existing reference_spool calls the new shared owner, so that comparison alone is not claimed to establish old semantics.

Independently reconstructed both complete candidates from the fetched base bodies. Oracle has exactly the one reviewed production replacement plus the 4498-byte appended test module. Streaming has exactly four reviewed replacements; all remaining bytes match the base. V2 differs from V1 only by the test method-call closure.
